artifacts.summary: Research on adding a lean Rust extension modeled on the python/nix extensions: recommended file set, cargo-based verification loop, and a well-motivated decision to omit an MCP server and a dedicated rules file.

memory_candidates.content: When adding a new language extension to agent-system/extensions/, use the python extension (not nix) as the lean base template: no rules/ file, no MCP server, no hooks/scripts, no settings-fragment.json -- only manifest.json, EXTENSION.md, README.md, index-entries.json, opencode-agents.json, two agents, two skills, and an optional short context/project/<lang>/README.md. Only add nix-style extras (MCP server, hooks, rules file, deep context tree) when a language-specific condition independently motivates them (e.g. a single community-converged MCP server, a foreign syntax needing deep docs, or conventions not mechanically auto-enforced by the language's own formatter/linter).

The Rust MCP-server ecosystem (crates-mcp, docsrs-mcp, rust-analyzer-mcp/rust-mcp, cargo-mcp) as of 2026 is fragmented across small community crates with no single converged/blessed server comparable to mcp-nixos for Nix. Do not default-bundle one into a new extension; WebSearch/WebFetch against docs.rs/crates.io is an adequate substitute, matching how the python extension already covers docs.python.org/PyPI without an MCP server.
